title: Early acoustic recording: megaphones, three masters and wax
summary: Howard describes five straight days of recording, playing through megaphones, making three masters and the razor-shaved wax.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well, he said it would take two weeks, but we rehearsed on the train going to win. One half of that car, when we were in the, I don't remember what they called it, buffet car maybe. Yes. In those days. Yes. And we stayed in there and got permission after the thing closed and we practiced, you know. We made these records, but it was about five days. Straight five days.
What kind of tunes did you, I heard some of those.
All of his numbers, I guess. Yeah.
Big band, huh?
Yeah.
How many pieces in the band?

Well, 14, I guess, 15, something like that. Nelson, what's his name, Kincaid. They had two clarinets, King Phillips and Nelson Kincaid. I don't remember the other violin player Handy brought here with him. They had three fiddles in the band.
Two clarinets, three fiddles, and what kind of other instruments?
Well, Handy played cornet and trombone. Jasper Taylor on drums. You could only use the snares. And I don't remember whether they had a tube or not. That's a long time ago.
Where were the records made?
At the Columbia Steelers, New York. Don't ask the address, please. I don't know.
What kind of a studio was it?
Well, we played through megaphones.
How many megaphones were there?
How many what? How many megaphones did they have?
Three. Three. Everybody had to be picked up on three different megaphones, is that it?

And they stopped me two, three times. My boy kept hitting the megaphones. I'm not lying. The guy with two clarinet said, what's the matter? I said, what's the matter? He says, well, you hit it again. I'm trying to be clear back. He used to be some nice and plunk. Real loud, you know.
Could you play back a take in those days and hear what you were doing?
Oh, yeah. Yeah. They would play it back for you? Oh, yeah. Sure. That's the days when they said, now we'll make a good one. You know?
Uh-huh.
And you'd make three masters. Supposedly three masters. They'd select the best out of the three.
Oh, I see. You made everything three times.

Uh-huh. I see. Wax that thick. Yes. That thick. Oh. The amusing part about it, the ones that you'd make your test over, they had this razor blade adjustment with an electric fan. And it just shaved that impression off.
Lose it over again.
Yeah. Always. Just shaved it off real fine. I see. Those days of the killer, I'm telling you.
